findings.recommendation: Move SpendGroupBatch (and _by_spend_group if shared) into a small module next to the repository, or into the same new module as GroupedRows (see CR-002), and import it into spend_logs_repository.py.

findings.title: AND evaluates every child, not selective-first
findings.problem: The spec requires an AND to evaluate its most selective ==/IN child first as an index lookup and test the remaining children only on those candidate groups. GroupedRows._compute evaluates every AND child in full ([self._evaluate(child) for child in node.clauses]); _intersection only sorts the finished sets by size afterwards.
findings.impact: A spec requirement is only partially met. The cost bound holds today only because the common term is memoised and already applied in the SQL WHERE; any filter with a broad non-common conjunct pays a full index lookup per row, so the per-batch cost guarantee is not structural.
findings.recommendation: In the "and" case, evaluate the most selective ==/IN child first as an index lookup, then test the remaining children only on those candidate rows instead of evaluating each child in full; keep the per-batch memoisation, and extend TestCostFollowsTheMatches with an AND whose second child is broad so the selective-first path is pinned.
findings.check_notes: GroupedRows._conjunction seeds on the most selective =/IN (or memoised) operand and tests the rest per candidate row; new test pins visits == 2*GROUPS

fix.change: GroupedRows AND looks up its most selective =/IN (or memoised) operand, sized without touching rows, then tests remaining operands only on its candidate rows; columns still validated up front

findings.title: read_group_spend docstring omits required timeout cause
findings.problem: The spec requires both the read_group_spend docstring and the module docstring to name a SPEND_LEDGER_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS timeout (dedicated pool only, SPEND_LEDGER_POOL_SIZE>0) as one cause of a blanked batch. Only the module docstring names it, as 'on the dedicated pool' without the POOL_SIZE>0 condition; the read_group_spend docstring does not mention it.
findings.impact: A spec requirement is partially met: a maintainer reading the function contract is not told that one statement timeout blanks the whole table, nor when that timeout applies.
findings.recommendation: Name the SPEND_LEDGER_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS timeout (dedicated pool only, SPEND_LEDGER_POOL_SIZE>0) as one cause of a blanked batch in the read_group_spend docstring, and add the SPEND_LEDGER_POOL_SIZE>0 condition to the module docstring's existing mention, in one short clause each.
findings.check_notes: read_group_spend and module docstrings both name SPEND_LEDGER_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS, dedicated pool only (SPEND_LEDGER_POOL_SIZE > 0)

fix.change: read_group_spend docstring names a SPEND_LEDGER_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS timeout (dedicated pool only, SPEND_LEDGER_POOL_SIZE > 0) as a cause of a blanked batch; module docstring gains the POOL_SIZE > 0 condition

findings.title: AC-13 statement test lacks project-row batch
findings.problem: AC-13 requires the statement for 1 and 10,000 filters to be identical and to contain no row's keys, aliases, projects or owners. test_ten_thousand_filters_issue_the_statement_one_filter_does builds only user rows sharing the common projects term (_rows_sharing); no project-row batch, where each row carries its own projects and personal_project_owners, is compiled.
findings.impact: The acceptance criterion is only partially covered: a regression that leaks per-row project names or owners into the grouped statement (which would grow the SQL with the table and break the one-statement design for projects-spending and CLI per-project tables) would pass the suite.
findings.recommendation: Add a project-table case to TestTheBatchedReadIsOneStatementWhateverTheRowCount: build 1 and 10,000 rows that each carry their own projects and personal_project_owners under a users-term common filter, render both through rendered_batch, assert the statements are identical and that no row's project names or owners appear in the SQL.
findings.check_notes: project-row test compiles 1 and 10,000 rows under a users-term common filter with literal binds; asserts identical SQL and no row project/owner

fix.change: Added project-row batch case: 1 and 10,000 rows with own projects and owners under a users-term common filter compile to the identical statement naming no row

findings.title: AC-1 non-admitted case compared to a literal
findings.problem: AC-1 requires the batched read to equal per-filter aggregate_by_spend_group for a non-admitted period. test_a_rejected_range_yields_no_figure_for_every_filter_without_a_read asserts against a literal no_figure dict instead of the single read for each filter.
findings.impact: The acceptance criterion is only partially covered: if the single read's non-admitted answer ever differs from a bare no_figure (for example a label or flag), the batched and single reads diverge and this test still passes, breaking the task's 'figures and flags identical' requirement unnoticed.
findings.recommendation: Compare the batched result for the non-admitted range with aggregate_by_spend_group called per filter on the same ledger (as AC-1 requires), keeping the assertion that no read was made.
findings.check_notes: non-admitted case now asserts the batched result equals aggregate_by_spend_group per filter and that the batch made no read

fix.change: Non-admitted range test compares the batched result with aggregate_by_spend_group per filter, keeping the no-read assertion
